title: Initialize shadcn/ui in the project
description: Initialize shadcn/ui using the CLI and install the core components needed throughout the admin dashboard. shadcn/ui copies components into the project — they are not a dependency. This provides the building blocks (tables, forms, dialogs, dropdowns, sidebars, badges, buttons, etc.) for all admin UI.
acceptanceCriteria: `components.json` exists at project root with shadcn/ui configuration
Core components are installed: button, badge, card, dialog, dropdown-menu, form, input, label, select, separator, sheet, sidebar, table, tabs, textarea, toast
shadcn/ui components import successfully without TypeScript errors
Tailwind CSS configuration supports shadcn/ui CSS variables

steps.details: Run `npx shadcn@latest init`. When prompted: choose Default style, select base color (Slate or Neutral), confirm the global CSS file (app/globals.css), confirm tailwind.config, confirm components path as `src/components/ui`. This creates `components.json`.

Run: `npx shadcn@latest add button badge card dialog dropdown-menu form input label select separator sheet sidebar table tabs textarea`. Install each or all at once. These are the core components needed for the admin dashboard.
Run: `npx shadcn@latest add progress avatar tooltip popover command`. These are needed for the batch status progress indicators, palette picker, and search/command palette.
Import `Button` from `@/components/ui/button` in any test file and confirm it renders without errors. Check that `src/components/ui/` contains the installed component files.

technicalNotes: shadcn/ui components are copied into the project — they live in src/components/ui/ and can be customized freely.
shadcn/ui requires Tailwind CSS to be configured. Since Tailwind 4.2.1 is already installed, the init should detect it automatically.
If using Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui may require additional configuration — check the shadcn/ui docs for v4 compatibility.
The `cn()` utility function from `src/lib/utils.ts` is installed by shadcn/ui and used for conditional class names.
